headline: S&P 500 jumps 2.4 percent, best day since April, as oil slides on Iran deal hopes
subhead: Brent fell 6.0 percent to 92.41 dollars and the Nasdaq rose 2.7 percent, but Nvidia lost 4.3 percent on its board's probe into CEO Jensen Huang; US October CPI is due today.

us.text: The S&P 500 rose 2.4 percent to 7,549.9, its best day since April 8, and the Nasdaq 2.7 percent as cheaper oil and a chip rebound lifted all 11 sectors.
Nvidia fell 4.3 percent after its board opened a probe into CEO Jensen Huang's ties to an alleged Chinese spy, while AMD jumped 13.3 percent.
The 10-year yield held near 4.86 percent before today's October CPI, with strong payrolls keeping traders leaning toward a December Fed hike.

india.text: The Nifty rose 0.1 percent to 25,044.65 and Bank Nifty closed at 59,741.25 as PSU banks rallied on softer crude, while IT stocks lagged.
FIIs net bought 7,212 crore rupees of shares on 9 November while DIIs net sold 7,173 crore, per provisional exchange data.
The rupee firmed 5 paise to 93.93 per dollar on softer crude and foreign inflows; Indian markets are shut today for a holiday.

global.text: Asia rallied in Tuesday trade, with the Nikkei up 5.1 percent and Kospi 4.5 percent as the US chip rebound spread; Samsung rose 5.8 percent.
Europe's STOXX 600 closed at 656.52 on Monday in a broad rally led by banks and defence stocks.
Brent fell 6.0 percent to 92.41 dollars, its lowest since August, as Qatar took an Iranian plan to reopen Hormuz to the White House.

weekly.narrative: The US midterms set the tone: a relief rally on Wednesday gave way to Thursday's AI chip rout on fears a Democratic Congress curbs data center building, and Friday's partial rebound and a 165,000 payrolls beat still left the S&P 500 down 2.7 percent and the Nasdaq 3.4 percent on the week. India went the other way, with foreign buying and cheaper crude lifting the Nifty 8.6 percent on the week and above 25,000 on Friday, while Kospi and the Nikkei bore the brunt of the chip selloff. Hopes of an Iran deal drove WTI down 12.8 percent on the week, and gold rose 4.5 percent and silver 5.5 percent despite rising Fed hike bets, while Bitcoin slipped 3.4 percent. Next week brings US CPI on 10 November, India CPI on 12 November and a reported start to Anthropic's IPO roadshow.
